themes.label: Stylized facts motivating long-memory volatility models
themes.need: Someone choosing between long-memory volatility model classes needs the stylized facts (persistent autocorrelation, fat tails, tail crossover, scaling/multiscaling) that motivate long-memory modeling and the practical/interpretive limitations of fractionally-integrated approaches (FIGARCH, ARFIMA) that motivate an alternative.
themes.distributed_justification: b001-b002 form one continuous motivation narrative; the gap at lines 17-18 is Pass-A trash (acknowledgment footnote), not a thematic break.

themes.label: Integrated variance and realized volatility notation across horizons
themes.need: Someone implementing a realized-volatility model needs the continuous-time price/integrated-variance notation, the realized-volatility estimator definition (eq. 3), and how it is aggregated to weekly/monthly horizons (eq. 4) for cross-horizon comparison.

themes.label: HAR-RV cascade model: economic motivation and derivation
themes.need: Someone wanting to specify a heterogeneous-component volatility model needs the economic motivation (Heterogeneous Market Hypothesis, trader-horizon heterogeneity) and the additive volatility-cascade derivation leading to the tractable HAR(3)-RV regression form (eq. 6-8).

themes.label: Simulation study reproducing volatility stylized facts
themes.need: Someone assessing whether HAR-RV can reproduce known volatility stylized facts (fat tails, tail crossover, long-memory autocorrelation, self-similarity) needs the simulation design (calibrated parameters, comparison against USD/CHF data), the kurtosis-crossover comparison, and the autocorrelation/persistence match to real data.
themes.distributed_justification: b009-b013 form one continuous simulation-results narrative (setup, distributional match, persistence match); the interior gaps are Pass-A trash (figure/table captions), not thematic breaks.

themes.label: Empirical HAR(3) estimation and forecast accuracy diagnostics
themes.need: Someone wanting to validate the HAR(3)-RV specification against real high-frequency data needs the dataset description (USD/CHF, S&P500, T-Bond tick data), the OLS/Newey-West in-sample estimation results with the goodness-of-fit comparison (F-test, AIC, BIC) against the unrestricted AR(22) benchmark, together with the resulting one-day-ahead forecast accuracy (RMSE/MAE/R2 vs. AR(1), AR(3), ARFIMA(5,d,0), via Mincer-Zarnowitz regressions) and the residual-heteroskedasticity caveat - the estimation is only validated once its forecasting performance is checked.

themes.label: Out-of-sample multi-horizon forecast comparison
themes.need: Someone evaluating HAR(3)'s out-of-sample multi-horizon forecasting performance against long-memory ARFIMA and short-memory AR alternatives needs the moving-window reestimation setup, the 1-day/1-week/2-week RMSE-MAE-R2 results (Table 5), the multistep Mincer-Zarnowitz regression form (eq. 12), and the explanation for why short-memory models underperform at longer horizons.
themes.distributed_justification: b021-b024 and the first part of b025 (327-329) form one continuous out-of-sample forecasting narrative (setup, results, horizon-dependent explanation); the interior gaps are Pass-A trash (figure captions), and the resplit at line 330 separates the horizon explanation from the practical-tradeoff discussion (see t08).

themes.label: HAR vs. ARFIMA practical tradeoff and conclusions
themes.need: Someone deciding whether to adopt HAR(3) or ARFIMA in practice, beyond raw forecast accuracy, needs the comparable-performance caveat and the practical-implementation tradeoff (HAR's simplicity and robustness on a moving window vs. ARFIMA's sensitivity to cutoff/frequency choices), together with the paper's summary of the HAR-RV model and its possible extensions.

resplits.reason: split test: two self-standing needs bundled in one block - the short-memory-underperformance explanation (continues the out-of-sample forecast narrative, t07) vs. the practical HAR-vs-ARFIMA implementation tradeoff (joins the conclusions, t08).
